title: Repeated failed administrator logons from single external IP (115.247.157.74) — likely brute-force

mitre.description: Attempt to gain access by repeatedly guessing passwords for accounts (brute-force).

notes: High-volume failed attempts from a single external IP against a privileged account strongly indicates automated brute-force. Recommend blocking the IP and checking for account lockouts and authentication policy gaps (e.g., missing MFA).

title: High-volume multi-account failed logons from multiple external IPs — credential stuffing / password spraying
description: At ~2025-11-19 21:37–21:39 UTC there is a dense burst of LogonFailed events for a large set of usernames (administrator, guest and many other account names) originating from multiple distinct external IPs (185.156.73.173, 92.63.197.9, 185.156.73.169, 185.156.73.24, 92.63.197.69, etc.). mitre.description: Attempts to gain account access by trying commonly used passwords across many accounts (password spraying) or using breached credential lists across accounts (credential stuffing).

indicators_of_compromise: many targeted account names (administrator, admin, guest, user, etc.)
notes: Multiple source IPs and many account names in a short interval are classic for distributed credential stuffing or spray. Prioritize blocking listed IPs, enforce/verify MFA for affected accounts, and search other systems for the same source IPs and any successful logons immediately after this burst.

title: Windows Defender exclusions added for Temp path, ProgramData cache and broad file extensions (possible defense evasion)
description: Registry values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions were created setting folder, extension and process exclusions on device azuki-sl within the requested time window. Entries include a user Temp path (C:\Users\KENJI~1.SAT\AppData\Local\Temp), C:\ProgramData\WindowsCache, broad extensions (.bat, .ps1, .exe) and process exclusions (mm.exe, svchost.exe). All changes were initiated by the system account with msmpeng.exe as the initiating process. Excluding Temp and adding broad executable/script extensions is a common defensive-evasion technique used to permit malware persistence and execution without detection. Although msmpeng.exe is a legitimate Defender component, the combination of broad extension exclusions, process exclusions and Temp-path exclusion is anomalous and warrants investigation (could be misconfiguration, policy push, or malicious tampering).

mitre.sub_technique: T1562.001 (Disable or Modify Security Tools) ; T1112 (Modify Registry)
mitre.description: Modifying Defender exclusion registry keys to allow files/processes to run without scanning (impair defenses) and creating persistent allowances via registry.

notes: msmpeng.exe is the Windows Defender service binary — this activity could be from a legitimate Defender update or management policy. However: (1) excluding Temp and broad executable/script extensions and processes is uncommon and high-risk; (2) confirm whether these exclusions were pushed via central management (Intune/GPO) or were local actions. Check for dropped files, scheduled tasks, or services that leverage the excluded paths/process names and validate endpoint agent integrity.

title: External payload downloads from litter.catbox.moe observed on azuki devices
description: Multiple explicit curl/wget command lines show downloads of .7z payloads from litter.catbox.moe to azuki hosts (azuki-adminpc and azuki-backupsrv). These are direct ingress/tool-transfer actions using an external anonymous file host — common technique to stage malware. The download commands write to C:\Windows\Temp\cache and temp .7z files.

mitre.description: Ingress of tools or payloads from external infrastructure (download of malicious files)

notes: Download targets are anonymous file hosting (catbox). Given the timeframe and presence of other suspicious activity, treat these downloads as likely malicious staging.

title: Multiple exfiltration uploads to gofile.io from azuki-adminpc
description: Several curl POST upload commands transfer likely sensitive archives to store1.gofile.io (gofile.io). Log entries show staged local files (credentials.tar.gz, banking-records.tar.gz, quickbooks-data.tar.gz, chrome-session-theft.tar.gz, etc.) POSTed to the remote service — clear exfiltration to an external file-hosting site via HTTPS.

mitre.description: Exfiltration of data via web-based file hosting using HTTP(S); use of application layer protocols for data transfer

indicators_of_compromise: filenames: credentials.tar.gz, quickbooks-data.tar.gz, banking-records.tar.gz, chrome-session-theft.tar.gz, chrome-credentials.tar.gz
notes: Multiple distinct sensitive-sounding archives were uploaded. Correlate with DLP/e-mail logs and host artifacts. Files uploaded to anonymous file hosts are high-priority for containment.

title: Lateral movement via PsExec from azuki-adminpc to internal hosts and execution of silentlynx.exe
description: Multiple ConnectionSuccess events show PsExec64.exe usage on azuki-adminpc to remote internal IPs (10.1.0.188, 10.1.0.204) executing 'silentlynx.exe' and other payloads with provided credentials. This indicates authenticated lateral execution (remote service/RPC), consistent with lateral movement and remote command execution.

mitre.sub_technique: Windows Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares (PsExec)
mitre.description: Use of PsExec/SMB to execute programs on remote systems and command execution via remote services

notes: PsExec usage combined with file staging (silentlynx.exe) strongly indicates adversary lateral movement activity. Confirm credential usage and identify compromised accounts (e.g., kenji.sato) and sessions associated with yuki.tanaka.

title: Unauthorized local account created and added to Administrators via encoded PowerShell
description: At 2025-11-25T04:51:10Z an encoded PowerShell command was executed which immediately created a new local account (yuki.tanaka2) and then added it to the local Administrators group. Encoded PowerShell indicates intentional obfuscation. The activity is consistent with an attacker establishing persistence and escalating privileges on azuki-adminpc under the compromised account yuki.tanaka.

mitre.description: Create local account and add to local Administrators (account manipulation). Encoded PowerShell indicates command obfuscation/execution via PowerShell (T1059.001).

notes: Remove yuki.tanaka2 and investigate where credentials may have been reused. Check for additional persistence mechanisms created for that account.

title: Post-exploitation interactive shell / Meterpreter observed (credential discovery & host recon)
description: A meterpreter payload executed on azuki-adminpc and issued reconnaissance commands (systeminfo, whoami /all). This is post-exploitation activity consistent with an interactive backdoor used to enumerate host and privileges.

mitre.description: Interactive shell/command execution (meterpreter) and system/user enumeration.

notes: Search network for other Meterpreter artifacts and C2 connections. Collect memory image from azuki-adminpc for further analysis before remediation if feasible.

title: External tool download and Chrome credential theft followed by exfiltration
description: Sequence shows download of an archive from litter.catbox.moe, extraction, running a tool to extract Chrome DPAPI-protected credentials, archiving the stolen artifacts, and uploading to an external file service (gofile.io). This is credential theft + exfiltration via public file hosting.

mitre.description: Ingress tool transfer (download of tools), execution of credential-stealing tool (dpapi chrome extraction), collection and exfiltration to an external HTTP-based file service.

indicators_of_compromise: Files: m-temp.7z, m.exe, chrome-real-dump.txt, Chrome-Cookies.db, chrome-session-theft.tar.gz
notes: Preserve copies of the downloaded archive and extracted tools if still present. Block the domains and hashes (if available) and search telemetry for any other hits to those URLs.

title: Ransomware-style preparation: backup deletion, AV/service stoppage, event log clearing, persistence
description: Between ~05:58 and 06:10 there are multiple commands disabling backup and security features, stopping services, deleting shadow copies, clearing event logs, disabling recovery, resizing shadow storage, creating a scheduled task for silentlynx.exe, and deleting backup catalogs. These are classic pre-encryption actions used by ransomware operators to prevent recovery and evade detection.

mitre.description: Inhibit system recovery (vssadmin, wbadmin), disable/stop security tools/services (net stop WinDefend/NisSrv/MpCmdRun/MsMpEng), clear event logs (wevtutil), create scheduled task for persistence (schtasks).

notes: Immediate containment recommended. Collect forensic artifacts (pre- and post-incident) if possible (disk and memory). Search other hosts for signs of silentlynx.exe and the scheduled task name.

title: Lateral movement observed via PsExec to internal hosts with credentialed accounts
description: PsExec64.exe was used to push and execute silentlynx.exe on multiple internal IPs with explicit -u and -p credentials, indicating credential-based lateral movement and remote command execution to hosts 10.1.0.102, 10.1.0.188, 10.1.0.204. The presence of plaintext/visible passwords in commands (redacted in logs) indicates credential theft/use.

mitre.description: Remote execution (PsExec) using valid accounts. Use of stolen/valid credentials for lateral movement.

notes: Force reset/disable accounts used (kenji.sato, fileadmin) pending investigation and search for credential reuse across environment. Scan the remote targets for silentlynx.exe and other artifacts.

title: Use of many native signed utilities (LOLBins) for malicious purposes
description: Multiple signed Windows tools and common admin utilities were used maliciously (curl.exe, 7z.exe, tar.exe, net.exe, vssadmin.exe, wbadmin, wevtutil.exe, bcdedit.exe, schtasks.exe, fsutil.exe, taskkill.exe). These legitimate binaries were used to download tools, extract archives, exfiltrate data, stop services, clear logs, and create persistence — a classic LOLBin abuse pattern.

mitre.description: Living-off-the-land binaries and scripts executed to perform malicious actions and evade detection.

indicators_of_compromise: LOLBins observed: curl.exe, 7z.exe, tar.exe, net.exe, vssadmin.exe, wbadmin, wevtutil.exe, bcdedit.exe, schtasks.exe, fsutil.exe, taskkill.exe
Use contexts: download, extract, credential theft, stop services, clear logs, create scheduled task
notes: Hunt for these binaries executing unusual command-lines across other endpoints. Consider restricting or monitoring use of administrative binaries from non-admin interactive sessions.

title: Data staging and potential hosting service use (FileZilla GUI observed; public file uploads used for exfil)
description: FileZilla server GUI was executed on azuki-adminpc and exfiltration to public file-hosting (gofile.io) was used for stolen Chrome data. FileZilla GUI may indicate setup of a hosting/staging service; combined with HTTP POST to gofile.io, this suggests multiple exfil methods were used.

mitre.description: Use of public file hosting for data exfiltration and potential hosting services used to stage or transfer data.

notes: Confirm whether FileZilla GUI was legitimately installed. Look for incoming/outgoing connections to FileZilla and search network logs for uploads to gofile.io and catbox.moe.

title: Local account created and added to Administrators via encoded PowerShell
description: At 2025-11-25T04:51:10Z a PowerShell encoded command was used to run net.exe to create a new local account 'yuki.tanaka2' and immediately add it to the local Administrators group. This is a common post-compromise action to obtain persistent administrative access on the host.

mitre.technique: Create Account / Add to Local Group
mitre.description: Attacker created a local user and added it to Administrators via PowerShell-encoded commands and net.exe.

notes: Encoded PowerShell used to mask account creation; treat yuki.tanaka2 as attacker-controlled and reset credentials + remove account after containment.

title: Browser credential theft and archive created
description: A staged tool ('m.exe') executed a dpapi chrome extraction against Chrome user data, produced a theft text/file, then attacker archived the output and uploaded it to an external file hosting service. This is explicit credential harvesting and exfiltration of browser-stored credentials/sessions.

mitre.technique: Credentials from Web Browsers / Exfiltration Over Web
mitre.description: DPAPI-based Chrome credential extraction followed by tar and HTTP POST upload to public file host.

recommendations: isolate azuki-adminpc and any storage with chrome data
collect memory image and browser profile for forensic analysis
notes: Treat any tokens/passwords in Chrome as compromised; rotate credentials and invalidate tokens (SSO, web apps).

title: Staging and execution of additional malicious binaries (m-temp.7z, silentlynx.exe)
description: The host downloaded an archive from an external URL (litter.catbox.moe), extracted it, then executed binaries (m.exe, silentlynx.exe). A cache path C:\Windows\Temp\cache\silentlynx.exe was used and later executed via PsExec to remote hosts. This chain indicates staging of custom malicious tools.

mitre.technique: Signed Binary Proxy Execution/Command and Scripting Interpreter / Remote Services
mitre.sub_technique: T1059 (Command and Scripting), T1021 (Remote Services - PsExec)
mitre.description: Download via curl, extraction with 7z, execution of dropped binaries and use of PsExec for lateral execution.

recommendations: pivot to listed remote IPs for containment and forensics
notes: Check endpoint file system snapshots for m-temp.7z, silentlynx.exe, and extracted artifacts; collect copies for analysis.

title: Defense evasion and anti-forensics observed (VSS deletion, AV/service stop, event log clearing, USN journal deletion)
description: Multiple commands that disable system recovery and attempt to remove traces were executed: vssadmin delete shadows, wbadmin delete catalog, bcdedit to disable recovery, vssadmin resize, stop Windows Defender, taskkill of AV processes, fsutil deletejournal, wevtutil clear of System/Application/Security/PowerShell logs, and creation of scheduled task for persistence. This is consistent with ransomware pre-encryption or post-compromise anti-forensics.

mitre.technique: Inhibit System Recovery / Delete Volume Shadow Copies / Disable Security Tools / Indicator Removal
mitre.sub_technique: T1490 (Inhibit System Recovery), T1070.001 (Clear Windows Event Logs), T1562.001 (Disable/Modify Security Tools)
mitre.description: Attacker removed shadow copies, disabled recovery, stopped AV/services, and cleared event logs to impede recovery and detection.

recommendations: isolate and preserve volatile data (memory) immediately
search endpoints for cleared logs and shadow copy deletions, and preserve VSS metadata if possible
notes: Immediate forensic preservation required — event logs and shadow copies likely wiped; check central backups and other hosts for copies.

title: Lateral movement attempts via PsExec and SSH; multiple remote hosts targeted
description: The user invoked PsExec64 to execute the staged 'silentlynx.exe' on multiple internal IPs using different credentials. There is also an SSH connection attempt to backup-admin@10.1.0.189. These are active lateral movement attempts to spread and execute payloads on other systems.

mitre.description: Uses PsExec and SSH to push and run a payload on internal hosts and access other systems.

recommendations: collect authentication logs for accounts used (kenji.sato, fileadmin, backup-admin)
notes: Search for successful remote execution indicators on those internal hosts and isolate them if compromised.

title: Mass service and process termination consistent with ransomware/impact activity
description: The staged binary 'silentlynx.exe' and net/taskkill commands were used to stop backup/antivirus services and kill multiple database and user-facing processes (sqlservr.exe, oracle.exe, mysql.exe, mongodb.exe, postgres.exe, MsMpEng.exe, NisSrv.exe, WinDefend) — consistent with ransomware preparation (stopping backups/AV and terminating apps before encryption).

mitre.technique: Stop or Disable Security/Backup Services; Terminate Processes
mitre.description: Stopping backup and security services and killing application processes to prevent recovery and detection.

recommendations: immediately snapshot/event-collect affected hosts and services
search for file-system changes consistent with mass encryption
indicators_of_compromise: taskkill /F /IM sqlservr.exe / oracle.exe / mysql.exe / mongodb.exe / postgres.exe
notes: Check for mass file renames/encryption activity and examine EDR for file write spikes immediately after these commands.

title: Interactive reconnaissance and C2-like activity (meterpreter, systeminfo, whoami, ssh)
description: A 'meterpreter.exe' process ran local discovery commands (systeminfo, whoami /all). The presence of meterpreter and SSH sessions indicates interactive attacker C2 and reconnaissance on the host.

mitre.technique: System Information Discovery / Application Layer Protocol
mitre.sub_technique: T1082 (System Information Discovery), T1071 (Application Layer Protocols / HTTP/HTTPS, possibly Meterpreter over TCP)
mitre.description: Attacker executed Meterpreter and used it to run discovery commands; also used SSH which may indicate remote interactive control.

recommendations: collect network session logs and EDR telemetry for outbound C2
block known C2 destinations and inspect for additional hosts with meterpreter
notes: Meterpreter presence is strong evidence of attacker foothold. Gather network flows, check DNS logs and proxy logs for communications to suspicious domains/IPs.
